title: fix(editor): Show agent validation details in tooltips
body:
## Summary

- Show structured configuration issues in the disabled Preview and Publish tooltips.
- Reuse existing localized area labels and validation messages for required or invalid settings.
- Identify invalid tools, channels, skills, schedules, sub-agents, MCP servers, and vector stores.
- Exclude publish-only checks from the Preview tooltip.

## How to test

The Agents module must be enabled with `N8N_ENABLED_MODULES=agents`.

1. Create or open an agent with incomplete instructions, model, or credential settings.
2. Hover over the disabled Preview button.
3. Confirm that the tooltip lists each runtime issue and its affected area.
4. Hover over the disabled Publish button.
5. Confirm that the tooltip lists each publish issue and its affected area.
6. Add an invalid capability, such as a tool with a missing credential, and confirm that the tooltip identifies the affected capability area.
7. Run `pnpm test src/features/agents/__tests__/AgentBuilderHeader.test.ts src/features/agents/__tests__/AgentPublishButton.test.ts` from `packages/frontend/editor-ui`.

title: feat(API): Add git connections pull to import projects from working copy

title: OTel node.execute spans missing in queue mode due to traceparent persistence race

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

labels.name: status:team-assigned
labels.description: A team has been assigned the issue or PR

labels.name: team:lifecycle
labels.description: Issue is with the Lifecycle & Governance team

body:
### Bug Description

When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled (N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true) and n8n runs in queue mode, node.execute spans can be missing from the trace that shows the workflow.execute span, even though tracing works correctly in regular (non-queue) mode.

Root cause: WorkflowRunner.enqueueExecution() adds the job to the queue before it runs the workflowExecuteBefore lifecycle hook. That hook starts the main processs workflow.execute OTel span and persists its traceparent to the execution row, so the worker can parent its own span under it.

Because the job is added to the queue first, a worker can dequeue and start executing before the traceparent write finishes. When that happens, the workers onWorkflowStart looks up a traceparent that is not written yet, so the workers own workflow.execute span (and every node.execute span nested under it) ends up disconnected from the trace under the main processs span, making it look like the node spans are missing.

A fix that persists the traceparent before enqueueing the job is proposed in #36757.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run n8n in queue mode (EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue) with at least one worker process and Redis.
2. Enable OTel tracing:
   - N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true
   - N8N_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=<your OTLP collector, e.g. Jaeger on :4318>
   - N8N_OTEL_TRACES_INCLUDE_NODE_SPANS=true
   - N8N_OTEL_TRACES_PRODUCTION_ONLY=false
3. Execute a workflow with 2+ nodes after the trigger (webhook trigger, or manual execution with OFFLOAD_MANUAL_EXECUTIONS_TO_WORKERS=true).
4. In the trace viewer, look for the trace containing the workflow.execute span for that execution.
5. Because the race is timing-dependent, this may need several runs (or a fast/idle worker) to reproduce reliably; a slower or busier worker is less likely to hit the race window.

### Expected Behavior

The workflow.execute span for the execution should contain all of that executions node.execute spans nested underneath it, in the same trace, matching the behavior seen in regular (non-queue) mode.

### Debug Info

N/A

### Operating System

macOS 15 (Sequoia) - also expected on Linux container deployments running queue mode

### n8n Version

2.36.0 (self-built from master)

### Node.js Version

24.16.0

### Database

PostgreSQL (also reproducible with SQLite, though queue mode with SQLite is not officially supported)

### Execution Mode

queue

### Hosting

self-hosted

title: fix: Flag resolutions field in community node package.json vetting
body:
Fixes CE-2377

## Summary

Community node vetting relies on the `no-overrides-field` ESLint rule (CE-738) to reject a `package.json` that pins/replaces transitive dependencies. Yet `nodrel-dev/n8n-fedex-node` passed vetting despite doing exactly that.

**Root cause (CE-2377):** the rule only inspected the npm `overrides` key. The FedEx node used the **Yarn `resolutions`** field — the functional equivalent, which forces a transitive dependency to a maintainer-controlled version or an arbitrary tarball/git URL that never appears in the node's readable source. Because the rule never looked at `resolutions`, the ESLint layer emitted no finding and the node passed overall.

The other hypotheses were ruled out: the rule is registered, active, and reports at `error` severity; the failure wasn't being swallowed downstream and the node wasn't grandfathered. The gap was purely an incomplete field check.

## Changes

- `no-overrides-field` now checks both `overrides` and `resolutions`, reporting each field independently under the existing `overridesForbidden` message id.
- Updated the message text to name both fields and the supply-chain reason (a transitive dep can be forced to an arbitrary version/tarball).

Minimal change scoped to the failing test already on the branch; no rule config or plugin wiring changes were needed.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes test src/rules/no-overrides-field.test.ts` → 9 passed (the two new `resolutions` cases were red before the fix).
- `pnpm --filter @n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes typecheck` → clean.
- `eslint` on both changed files → clean.
- `biome format` → no changes.
- `pnpm mutate .../no-overrides-field.ts` → **91.30%** (above the 80% threshold). The 2 survivors are pre-existing guards (`context.filename.endsWith` L21, `node.parent?.type` L27) unrelated to this change; every mutant in the new `overrides`/`resolutions` loop is killed — the test is load-bearing. (Stryker is not hoisted for this non-onboarded package, so I temporarily symlinked it from the pnpm store to run `pnpm mutate`; those symlinks live under gitignored `node_modules` and the helper was deleted — the committed diff is the source change only.)

## Review checklist

- [x] Fix addresses the root cause identified in the ticket
- [x] Tests pass (including the previously failing cases)
- [x] Typecheck and lint pass
- [x] Mutation testing confirms the test is load-bearing

---

title: feat(core): Seed imported credentials from bundled expression values
body: ## Summary Stacked on #36754 (export side). This PR adds the import side of LIGO-987: a new `credentialMissingMode` value, `create-with-values`. - Under `create-with-values`, the import creates each missing credential and seeds it from the expression data the package bundles (`credential.json` `data`, produced by `credentialExportPolicy=expression-values-only`). A reference the package carries no data for falls back to an empty stub, exactly like `create-stub`. - Seeded credentials are reported in a new `credentials.seeded` array in the import result. They do not join the stub publish override, so the caller's `workflowPublishingPolicy` alone decides publishing. Empty fallback stubs keep today's `stub-credential` block. An integration test proves both paths in one import. - Matched or existing credentials are never merged or updated with bundled data. Create-path only. - Defence in depth: bundled credential files parse through the same schema the exporter writes with. A tampered package that carries a literal value fails the import with a schema validation error; a test covers this. - Bundle lookup is by credential id. The manifest rejects duplicate credential ids, so no scope-precedence logic is needed and cross-project ownership works unchanged. - `CredentialsService.createStubCredential` gains an optional `data` argument. It keeps skipping field validation, and passes the decrypted data through `save`, so external-secret-provider dependencies register for seeded `$secrets.*` references. - Telemetry: the `n8n-package-imported` event's created credential ids now include seeded creations. - The mode flows through all four layers: module, DTO, public API (handler + OpenAPI), CLI (`--credential-missing-mode=create-with-values`). ## How to test 1. On an instance with this branch, create a credential whose fields are expressions (for example `={{ $secrets.github.token }}`). 2. Export a workflow that uses it (default policy bundles the expression data). 3. Import the package into another project: `n8n-cli package import --file=export.n8np --credential-missing-mode=create-with-values`. 4. Check the result: the credential appears under `credentials.seeded`, the created credential carries the expression values, and the workflow publishes when the publishing policy asks for it. 5. Repeat with a package exported under `credentialExportPolicy=no-values`: the import creates an empty stub, lists it under `credentials.stubbed`, and blocks publishing with `stub-credential`. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/LIGO-987 Stacked on #36754. ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: experiment(NODE-5796): effort bake-off high-opus5 [do not merge]
body: Fixes NODE-5796 ## Summary Adds two failing tests that reproduce `TypeError: page.includes is not a function` in the Notion node's load-options path. **No fix is included** — this PR is the reproduction only. `extractPageId` declares its parameter as `page = ''`. A default parameter only applies when the argument is `undefined`, so every other non-string value — an object, `null`, a number — sails past the default and reaches `page.includes(...)`, which throws. The value gets there through a false type assertion. `getDatabaseIdFromPage` casts the result of `getCurrentNodeParameter('pageId', { extractValue: true })` with `as string` and hands it straight to `extractPageId`. But `pageId` on `databasePage:update` is a `resourceLocator` whose default is the object `{ mode: 'url', value: '' }`, so whenever extraction doesn't yield a string the raw object is what arrives — the cast silences the compiler without changing the runtime value. Note the sibling handler `getDatabaseOptionsFromPage` in the same file already guards this (`pageIdValue ?? ''` plus an early `return []` on a falsy page ID), which is a useful reference for what the fix should look like — though `?? ''` alone is not sufficient here, since it only catches `null`/`undefined` and not the resourceLocator object. ### Tests added **`nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts`** — a unit-level `test.each` asserting `extractPageId` does not throw for a resourceLocator object, `null`, or a number. **`nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts`** — a test over the real caller: `getDatabaseIdFromPage` is invoked with `pageId` set to the resourceLocator default `{ mode: 'url', value: '' }`, and is expected to return no options without issuing an API request. `notionApiRequest` is partially mocked (via `importActual`, so the real `extractPageId` still runs) to keep the test off the network. ### Current failure Exactly the reported error, on the reported call path: ``` FAIL nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts > Notion V2 load options > returns no options when the database page resource locator has not been filled in AssertionError: promise rejected "TypeError: page.includes is not a function" instead of resolving Caused by: TypeError: page.includes is not a function ❯ extractPageId nodes/Notion/shared/GenericFunctions.ts:785:11 ❯ Object.getDatabaseIdFromPage nodes/Notion/v2/methods/loadOptions.ts:129:17 ``` And the unit-level cases: ``` FAIL ... extractPageId with non-string values > should not throw for a resourceLocator object FAIL ... extractPageId with non-string values > should not throw for a number expected [Function] to not throw an error but 'TypeError: page.includes is not a function' was thrown FAIL ... extractPageId with non-string values > should not throw for null expected [Function] to not throw an error but 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'includes')' was thrown ``` ## Customer impact **How a customer reaches it.** Entirely through normal editor use, with no misconfiguration on their part. A user adds a Notion node, picks resource **Database Page** and operation **Update**, and opens the **Key Name or ID** dropdown before the **Database Page** field above it holds a resolvable page. That happens on essentially every fresh setup — the field starts empty, and users routinely open the properties dropdown to see what's available before, or while, filling in the page link. It is also reached when the page link is present but doesn't extract cleanly (a pasted URL in an unexpected shape, or an expression that hasn't resolved yet). **What they see.** The dropdown fails to load and shows an error instead of the page's property list, so there is no way to choose which property to update. The node cannot be configured for this operation — this is a hard block, not cosmetic: the user is stopped at configuration time and cannot complete the workflow they came to build. **Business consequence.** This is a high-volume, long-lived break: **5,319 events across 419 affected users**, first seen 2025-05-21 and still firing as of 2026-08-20 on `n8n@2.36.3` in production. The Notion "update a database page" flow is a common automation, so the blocked users are people actively trying to build something and abandoning it. Beyond the direct funnel loss and support burden, the failure surfaces as a raw `TypeError` rather than a handled validation message, which reads as instability in a first-party integration. It also generates sustained backend error noise that obscures other signals in monitoring. ## How to test ```bash cd packages/nodes-base pnpm test nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts pnpm test nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts ``` Both fail on this branch, by design. `nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts` reports `3 failed | 56 passed` — the 3 new cases fail and every pre-existing test still passes. To confirm the customer-facing path manually: add a Notion node, choose **Database Page → Update**, leave **Database Page** empty, and open the **Key Name or ID** dropdown. ## Assumptions - **Scope is the test only.** The task was to reproduce the bug, not fix it, so `extractPageId` and `getDatabaseIdFromPage` are untouched. - **Expected behaviour once fixed.** The load-options test asserts `getDatabaseIdFromPage` resolves to `[]` and issues no API request when the page ID can't be resolved. That mirrors `getDatabaseOptionsFromPage`'s existing contract in the same file rather than inventing a new one. A fix therefore needs both halves — make `extractPageId` non-string-safe *and* add the early return — which matches how the sibling function is written. - **Non-string cases covered.** The unit test covers object, `null`, and number, the three shapes named in the report. It asserts only "does not throw" and not a specific return value, to avoid constraining the fix's shape. - **`GET /healthz` in the Sentry event is unrelated** background health-check traffic tagged onto the event, not the triggering request. The real entry point is the load-options endpoint (`DynamicNodeParametersController.getOptions`), which is what the test exercises. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/NODE-5796 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` ## Verification | Command | Outcome | | --- | --- | | `pnpm test nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts` (in `packages/nodes-base`) | ❌ **Fails as intended** — `1 failed \| 1 passed`. Rejects with `TypeError: page.includes is not a function` at `GenericFunctions.ts` → `loadOptions.ts:129`, matching the reported stack trace. | | `pnpm test nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts` (in `packages/nodes-base`) | ❌ **Fails as intended** — `3 failed \| 56 passed`. Only the 3 new cases fail; no pre-existing test regressed. | | `pnpm typecheck` (in `packages/nodes-base`) | ✅ Passes, no output. | | `npx eslint nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts` | ✅ **0 errors.** 25 warnings, all pre-existing in `GenericFunctions.test.ts` (import ordering, `unbound-method`, `no-explicit-any` in existing fixtures) and none on added lines. The package `lint` script runs eslint with `--quiet`, which suppresses warnings. | | `npx biome check --write` on both files | ✅ `Checked 2 files. No fixes applied.` — already conforms to house style. | Note on tooling: `pnpm lint ` in `packages/nodes-base` ignores the path argument and lints the whole package (`eslint nodes credentials utils test`), which OOMs on this runner. I scoped eslint to the two changed files directly to get a clean signal — that is a limitation of the package script, not of the change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- 🐱 Opened by [cat-bot](https://github.com/n8n-io/cat-bot/actions/runs/32385332074). Review the changes; close if the approach is wrong.

title: fix: Retry the codespace skills install and add the security plugin (no-changelog)
body: ## Summary A codespace started without the `quality` skills and nothing said so. `/tmp/post-start.log` had the reason: ``` Adding marketplace…✘ Failed to add marketplace: Failed to clone marketplace repository: Cloning into '/home/node/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/n8n-io-n8n-agent-skills'... fatal: cannot copy '/usr/share/git-core/templates/description' to '.../n8n-io-n8n-agent-skills/.git/description': File exists ``` The `git ls-remote` probe on the line above it succeeded, so the `customizations.codespaces.repositories` grant was authorized — this was a clone that died partway through the loader's staging path, not the auth failure the README's troubleshooting predicts. `post-start.mjs` ran `marketplace add` exactly once and `tryRun` only logged the failure, so the container came up looking healthy while every session in it silently lacked the skills. Changes to `.devcontainer/codespaces/post-start.mjs`: - **Retry the marketplace add once**, clearing the loader's staging directory first so the retry starts from a clean path. - **Write `/tmp/post-start-status.json`** with the installed/failed plugin lists, matching the machine-readable-summary pattern `pnpm agent:setup` already uses. - **Print a banner** naming the missing plugins and the command to retry, so a skipped install isn't invisible until someone misses a skill mid-session. - **Install the `security` plugin** from the same marketplace alongside `quality`. `quality` (10 skills, 3 agents) and `security` (4 skills) together add ~5k always-on tokens per session; the README notes how to drop one if that budget matters more. ## How to test Both `marketplace add` and `plugin install` exit 0 when the marketplace or plugin is already present, so the script is safe to re-run: ```bash node /workspaces/n8n/.devcontainer/codespaces/post-start.mjs cat /tmp/post-start-status.json # {"installed":["quality@…","security@…"],"failed":[]} claude plugin list # both enabled, scope: user ``` Verified in this codespace: - **Happy path** — both plugins install; a second run is a no-op and stays exit 0. - **Recovery** — removed the marketplace, recreated the poisoned staging directory (`.git/description` present), re-ran. Worth noting for reviewers: **the loader self-healed** (`Found stale directory, cleaning up and re-cloning…`) and succeeded on the first attempt, so the retry never fired. Claude Code 2.1.237 already handles a stale directory, which means the original failure was transient rather than a permanent trap. The retry is still worth having — it turns a transient clone failure into a recovery instead of a silently skipped install — but it is belt-and-braces, not the load-bearing fix. The comments and README were corrected to say that rather than assert a mechanism I'd disproved. - **Failure reporting** — ran a copy of the script against a nonexistent repo: the retry fires, both attempts fail, the banner prints, and the status file records `failed`. No stray marketplace was left in user settings afterwards. `biome check` clean; `node --check` passes. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts None — found while debugging why the skills were missing in a live codespace. ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. - [x] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [ ] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: experiment(NODE-5796): effort bake-off xhigh-opus5 [do not merge]
body: Fixes NODE-5796 ## Summary Adds **failing** tests that reproduce a crash in the Notion node's load-options handler. No production code is changed — this PR is the reproduction, not the fix, so CI on this branch is expected to be red. `extractPageId` in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Notion/shared/GenericFunctions.ts` is declared as `extractPageId(page = '')` and immediately calls `page.includes('p=')`. A default parameter only applies to `undefined`, so any *other* non-string value — an object, a number, `null` — sails past the default and blows up on `.includes`. The value gets there through a false type assertion. `getDatabaseIdFromPage` (`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Notion/v2/methods/loadOptions.ts:129-131`) does: ```ts const pageId = extractPageId( this.getCurrentNodeParameter('pageId', { extractValue: true }) as string, ); ``` `pageId` is a `resourceLocator` whose default is the object `{ mode: 'url', value: '' }`. When extraction doesn't yield a string, that raw object is what arrives — the `as string` cast makes the compiler agree while the runtime disagrees. The sibling handler in the same file, `getDatabaseOptionsFromPage`, already guards this correctly (`if (!pageId) return []`); `getDatabaseIdFromPage` does not. ### Tests added **`nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts`** — a `describe('extractPageId with a non-string value')` block covering the root cause directly, parameterised over an unresolved resource locator object, an empty object, a number, and `null`. Each asserts the call does not throw and returns an empty id. **`nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts`** — the caller path. Mocks `notionApiRequest` (keeping `extractPageId` real via `importActual`, so the bug still reproduces) and calls `getDatabaseIdFromPage` with `pageId` set to the resource locator default. Expects `[]` and no API call, matching the established convention for this parameter in both the sibling v2 handler and the v3 equivalent. ### Assumptions - **Expected behaviour on the caller path is `[]` with no API request.** The ticket describes the crash, not the desired outcome, so this is inferred from the two neighbouring handlers that already handle "no page chosen" that way. A fixer who prefers a different shape should adjust this assertion. - **`''` is the expected return for a non-string id**, keeping `extractPageId` consistent with its own `page = ''` default so callers' falsy checks keep working. - Only the v2 path from the Sentry trace is covered here. `v3/methods/loadOptions.ts:129` uses `extractPageId(pageIdValue ?? '')`, where `??` likewise only guards `null`/`undefined` — the shared-function tests cover that root cause, but no v3-specific test was added since it isn't in the reported trace. ## How to test ```bash cd packages/nodes-base pnpm test nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts ``` The 5 new tests fail; the 57 pre-existing tests in those files pass. The failures reproduce the reported stack frame for frame: ``` FAIL nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts > returns no options when database keys are requested without a page TypeError: page.includes is not a function ❯ extractPageId nodes/Notion/shared/GenericFunctions.ts ❯ Object.getDatabaseIdFromPage nodes/Notion/v2/methods/loadOptions.ts:129:17 ``` ``` FAIL nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts > extractPageId with a non-string value > ... for an unresolved resource locator object ... AssertionError: expected [Function] to not throw an error but 'TypeError: page.includes is not a function' was thrown ``` The `null` case fails with the sibling message `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'includes')` — same defect, same line. ## Customer impact **How a customer reaches this state.** They add a Notion node, pick **Database Page → Update**, and open the **Properties** section to map a field. The **Key Name or ID** dropdown is wired to the `getDatabaseIdFromPage` load-options method and re-fetches whenever `pageId` changes. If the **Database Page** locator hasn't resolved to a usable value yet — it's still on its empty default, the URL hasn't been validated, or the field is driven by an expression the editor can't resolve at design time — the dropdown fires anyway with the raw locator object. Nothing unusual is required; this is the ordinary order of operations when configuring the node, which is why it's the top frame in a high-volume Sentry issue. **What they see.** The dropdown never populates. Instead of an empty list or a "choose a page first" state, the load-options request 500s and the editor surfaces an error, so the field appears broken rather than merely unfilled. body: Fixes NODE-5796 ## Summary Adds **failing** test coverage reproducing `TypeError: page.includes is not a function` in the Notion node's load-options path. **No fix is included** — this PR only demonstrates the bug. `extractPageId(page = '')` in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Notion/shared/GenericFunctions.ts:916` relies on a default parameter, which only guards `undefined`. Any other non-string value — an object, `null`, a number — reaches `page.includes(...)` on line 917 and throws. The caller `getDatabaseIdFromPage` (`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Notion/v2/methods/loadOptions.ts:129-131`) asserts the resolved parameter with `as string`: ```ts const pageId = extractPageId( this.getCurrentNodeParameter('pageId', { extractValue: true }) as string, ); ``` `pageId` is a `resourceLocator` whose default value is the object `{ mode: 'url', value: '' }` (`shared/descriptions/DatabasePageDescription.ts:591-594`). When `extractValue` does not yield a string, that object flows straight through the cast into `extractPageId`. The sibling handler `getDatabaseOptionsFromPage` already guards this case (`?? ''` plus an empty-`pageId` early return); `getDatabaseIdFromPage` does not. Two test locations, matching the two levels of the reported stack trace: - `nodes/Notion/test/GenericFunctions.test.ts` — direct `extractPageId` cases for a resource-locator object, `null`, and a number. - `nodes/Notion/test/v2/loadOptions.test.ts` — `getDatabaseIdFromPage` invoked with an unresolved resource locator, asserting the rejection is not a `TypeError`. `notionApiRequest` is mocked (via `importOriginal` so the real `extractPageId` is still exercised) so the test stays offline whichever way the bug is later fixed — early return or string coercion. Assumption stated for reviewers: the load-options assertion deliberately checks only "does not fail with a `TypeError`" rather than a specific return value, so it does not pre-commit the eventual fix to either an early `[]` return or coercion. ## Customer impact **(a) How a customer reaches this state:** Anyone editing a Notion node configured for **Database Page → Update**. The "Key Name or ID" dropdown is backed by the `getDatabaseIdFromPage` load-options handler, and the editor loads that dropdown as soon as the field is rendered — before the user has picked a page, or whenever the page URL they pasted does not match the extraction pattern. At that moment the `pageId` resource locator is still its default object, and the load-options request throws server-side. **(b) What they see and the business consequence:** The dropdown fails to populate — an error toast / red field where the list of database properties should be, with no indication of what to do about it.
